findings.explanation: Chrome did not retire third-party cookies: Google said in April 2025 it will keep its current third-party cookie choice approach. In October 2025 it announced it is retiring the Attribution Reporting API and Topics, so readers are told to migrate to APIs that are being removed.
findings.quote: Chrome Privacy Sandbox milestones through twenty twenty-four retire third-party cookies; migrate impression-assisted stitching plans toward Attribution Reporting API summaries and Topics enrichment
findings.suggested_fix: Say Chrome still supports third-party cookies by user choice (blocked by default in Incognito), and drop the advice to migrate to Attribution Reporting/Topics; recommend first-party and server-side identifiers instead.

findings.explanation: UC-23.1.6 is 'Mobile App Crash Rate and User Impact', not mobile attribution; 'UC-23.2.* AB&M variants' is not a resolvable reference.
findings.quote: Mobile-app-only attribution (use UC-23.1.6 with Firebase / Branch.io)
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the UC-23.1.6 pointer, or cite the UC that actually covers mobile attribution and the specific 23.2 ABM UC ID after looking it up.

findings.explanation: Dashboard Studio has `splunk.sankey` and `splunk.parallelcoordinates`, but no `splunk.matrix` or `splunk.radialGauge` types; gauges are `splunk.markergauge`/`splunk.fillergauge`/`splunk.singlevalueradial`, and heatmaps are usually `splunk.punchcard` or a coloured `splunk.table`.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with real types: `splunk.punchcard` or a heat-coloured `splunk.table` for channel × position, and `splunk.markergauge` or `splunk.singlevalueradial` for the confidence tile.

findings.explanation: The SPL computes no z-score, no drift and no baseline, and writing to `notable` implies Enterprise Security; the `last_run`/`count=72` values are invented.
findings.quote: emits per-channel attribution-drift findings written to `notable` with severity tied to z-score on 45-day baseline
findings.suggested_fix: Describe evidence the search actually produces: the per-channel attribution table (linear/first/last-touch revenue, conversions, average depth) archived per run, plus the Step 3 reconciliation against Adobe/GA4 totals.

findings.explanation: Step 2 promises U-shape, W-shape, time-decay and data-driven macros with no SPL, and the wording is near word salad; readers cannot build any of them from this text.
findings.quote: mta_time_decay applies foreach or Python-exported weights when you move Markov refinement outside streaming macros
findings.suggested_fix: Either provide working SPL for one or two extra models (e.g. U-shape via position-in-path weights after `mvexpand`) or state plainly that only linear, first-touch and last-touch are computed here.

findings.explanation: Generic scenarios that do not name real attribution distortions. Step 5 already lists the real ones: ITP/ATT identifier loss, consent revocation, identity-graph merge conflicts, ad-blocker SDK loss, offline conversion lag, bot organic touches.
findings.quote: Scheduled automation elevates `attributed_channel` without crossing `revenue_usd` > 0 for UC-23.1.5.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with those concrete causes and how each shows up in the output columns.

findings.explanation: The Splunk Add-on for Salesforce collects Salesforce platform objects and event logs; it is not documented to pull Marketing Cloud Personalization (Interaction Studio) data or emit `sfmc:is_session`.
findings.quote: Optional Splunk Add-on for Salesforce ([Splunkbase 3549](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/3549)) when Interaction Studio REST pulls feed Splunk through TA-governed inputs.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the add-on's supported inputs; if Interaction Studio is unsupported, describe a custom REST/HEC bridge instead.

findings.explanation: Verified by an automated agent with no SME sign-off while SPL outputs are fabricated constants.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade to draft/community pending SME review.

findings.explanation: Asterisk PBX, ServiceNow and syslog play no role in CDP-based journey attribution.
findings.suggested_fix: Limit equipment to sources actually used (db_connect, salesforce, snowflake).

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `| sort stitch_key _time` without a count limit returns at most 10,000 results, so 45 days of multi-CDP touch events are silently truncated before `streamstats` builds paths. Use `sort 0 stitch_key _time`.

`markov_removal_effect_mass` is computed as `revenue_usd*0.13/(depth-1)` or `revenue_usd*0.07`, which are arbitrary constants, not a Markov removal effect. `confidence_pct` is a hard-coded ladder (92/81/67/56/51) with no statistical basis. Output column names and `attrib_model_hint` labels ('mtp_deep_markov_shapley_review') present fabricated numbers as model outputs.

`streamstats current=f window=20 ... by stitch_key` never resets at a conversion, so touches before an earlier purchase are re-credited to later purchases. `revenue_first_touch`/`revenue_last_touch` are summed per expanded row, so a channel that repeats in the path is credited the full revenue several times. `dc(stitch_key) as attributed_conversions` counts buyers, not conversions.
`Performance, Reliability` does not describe a marketing attribution report; `Business`/`Analytics` fits the signal.

summary: An ambitious multi-CDP attribution UC whose SPL fabricates 'Markov removal effect' and 'confidence_pct' values from hard-coded constants and silently truncates to 10,000 events at `sort`. Prose overclaims model sophistication, cites retired Privacy Sandbox APIs and a cookie deprecation that never happened, points exclusions at an unrelated UC, and names Dashboard Studio visualization types that do not exist.
